title: Semi-Annual User Access review exclusion of dormant users with access
header: Semi-Annual User Access review exclusion of dormant users with access
issue:
The Semi-Annual User Access review performed in November 2025 does not include dormant users with active access within CoStar, resulting in an incomplete user listing.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-07 Section No. [10] - Semi-Annual User Access Certification — Dormant accounts with active access must be identified and recertified
2. S-07 Section No. [9] - Privileged User Access Recertification Review — Comprehensive user listing required for periodic recertification
originalIssue:
The Semi-Annual User Access review performed in November 2025 does not include dormant users with active access within CoStar, resulting in an incomplete user listing.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-07 Section No. [10] - Semi-Annual User Access Certification — Dormant accounts with active access must be identified and recertified
2. S-07 Section No. [9] - Privileged User Access Recertification Review — Comprehensive user listing required for periodic recertification
rootCause: The user access review process was not designed to include dormant users with active access within CoStar.
impact: Dormant users with active access could exploit or misuse the system, potentially leading to unauthorized transactions, data manipulation, or exposure of sensitive information.
recommendation:
1. Update the Semi-Annual User Access review process to identify and address dormant users with active access within CoStar.

2. Define criteria to identify dormant users based on a specified period of inactivity.

3. Revoke access for dormant users unless management provides and documents a valid business justification.

4. Management should implement a monitoring mechanism to periodically review and validate the effectiveness of the updated user access review process.

5. Train relevant personnel on the updated process to promote proper execution and accountability.
managementResponse: Management agrees with the finding. Global Access Management will update the CoStar semi-annual recertification charter to mandate automated identification and deprovisioning of accounts dormant beyond 90 days, with supervisory sign-off workflows.
summaryFinding: Semi-annual access recertification omitted dormant accounts across the CoStar ERP application, presenting an unauthorized privileged access risk across 140 active credentials.
auditorResponse: Internal Audit verified that 140 dormant user accounts remained enabled in CoStar for over 180 consecutive days without formal supervisory exception approval.
mitigatingControl: Compensating database monitoring query is executed monthly by IT Security, though automated deprovisioning was absent.
exceptionRemedComments: Management has initiated a system enhancement request (CR-8821) to automate account suspension after 90 days of inactivity.

title: DHL and HCL J&J network account disabling not within ten business days
header: DHL and HCL J&J network account disabling not within ten business days
testProcedure: TP-105: Third-Party Vendor Network Access Deprovisioning
issue:
An application security assessment for the MDG S4/HANA environment had not been completed at the time of review.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-15 Section No. [2] - Security Assessment for COTS Systems/Applications — Security assessment not completed for the environment
2. S-15 Section No. [11] - ISRM Approval Prior to Production — ISRM approval lacking due to missing assessment
3. S-15 Section No. [4.18] - Periodic Application Architecture/Code/Config Assessment — No periodic assessment of architecture, code, configuration
originalIssue:
An application security assessment for the MDG S4/HANA environment had not been completed at the time of review.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-15 Section No. [2] - Security Assessment for COTS Systems/Applications — Security assessment not completed for the environment
2. S-15 Section No. [11] - ISRM Approval Prior to Production — ISRM approval lacking due to missing assessment
3. S-15 Section No. [4.18] - Periodic Application Architecture/Code/Config Assessment — No periodic assessment of architecture, code, configuration
rootCause: The access deprovisioning process for third-party associates did not enforce and complete network account disablement within ten business days after employment termination or role changes, resulting in continued access contrary to IAPP S-07.
impact: Residual network access by transferred 3PL associates could enable them to view, modify, or delete J&J information and execute actions that do not meet management's intentions.
recommendation:
1. Implement automated HR termination feed integration into Active Directory for 3PL accounts.
2. Mandate bi-weekly access recertification audits for DHL & HCL personnel.
3. Enforce automatic account lock after 10 days of inactivity.
managementResponse: HR and IT IAM engineering have initiated webhook automation between Contractor Management and Active Directory queues.

summaryFinding: Third-party logistics personnel retained active network and Active Directory access beyond the mandatory 10-business-day deprovisioning window upon contract termination.

title: Catheter Line 3 optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2%
header: Catheter Line 3 optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2%
testProcedure: TP-103: Automated Telemetry & Calibration Logging Review
issue:
Optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2% tolerance threshold during continuous electrophysiology catheter assembly runs across 72 consecutive operating hours.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-12 Section No. [3.4] - Automated System Telemetry Logging & Monitoring — Sensor calibration drift exceeds acceptable operating tolerance limits
2. S-12 Section No. [8.1] - Hardware Integrity & Recalibration Protocols — Mandatory gain verification cycles omitted during multi-batch production
originalIssue:
Optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2% tolerance threshold during continuous electrophysiology catheter assembly runs across 72 consecutive operating hours.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-12 Section No. [3.4] - Automated System Telemetry Logging & Monitoring — Sensor calibration drift exceeds acceptable operating tolerance limits
2. S-12 Section No. [8.1] - Hardware Integrity & Recalibration Protocols — Mandatory gain verification cycles omitted during multi-batch production
rootCause: Thermal dissipation latency in cleanroom HVAC Unit 4 created secondary optic gain drift during peak batch cycles, causing uncompensated sensor offsets.
impact: Potential delay in batch release and risk of $120,000 material scrap variance if unmitigated. Non-compliance with FDA GxP 21 CFR Part 11 records.
recommendation:
1. Upgrade sensor firmware to v4.2 enabling auto thermal offset compensation.
2. Establish real-time telemetry threshold alerts on IT Monitoring Console.
3. Enforce dual MFA authorization for manual sensor override calibrations.
managementResponse: Engineering will deploy telemetry calibration firmware v4.2 across all Catheter lines by end of Q3.
summaryFinding: Automated optical sensor telemetry logs on Catheter Assembly Line 3 demonstrated thermal gain drift exceeding the 1.5% SLA tolerance across 72 hours of production.
auditorResponse: Telemetry data logs confirmed 14 distinct excursions where gain offsets triggered manual supervisor override without root-cause ticket generation.
mitigatingControl: Post-assembly optical inspection station filters finished catheter batches prior to sterilization, preventing defective batch release.
exceptionRemedComments: Cleanroom HVAC Unit 4 thermal balance valve replacement scheduled; firmware patch v4.2 in validation testing.
impactedMrc: MRC-01: Global Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations

title: Third-party vendor GxP access log retention policy non-compliance
header: Third-party vendor GxP access log retention policy non-compliance
testProcedure: TP-110: GxP Software Validation & Data Integrity Audit
issue:
Third-party vendor GxP software access logs were purged after 90 days instead of being retained for the mandatory 7-year regulatory period.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-19 Section No. [5] - GxP Audit Trail & Log Retention Policy — Purging access logs prior to the mandatory 7-year retention period violates compliance standards
2. S-19 Section No. [12] - Vendor Hosted Application Verification — Absence of contractual automated log archiving for third-party cloud platforms
originalIssue:
Third-party vendor GxP software access logs were purged after 90 days instead of being retained for the mandatory 7-year regulatory period.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-19 Section No. [5] - GxP Audit Trail & Log Retention Policy — Purging access logs prior to the mandatory 7-year retention period violates compliance standards
2. S-19 Section No. [12] - Vendor Hosted Application Verification — Absence of contractual automated log archiving for third-party cloud platforms
rootCause: Vendor cloud storage auto-archive rule was misconfigured during cloud migration, overwriting default 7-year retention policy.
impact: Potential audit finding under GxP data integrity rules. Inability to substantiate historic access logs during external regulatory inspections.
recommendation:
1. Reconfigure cloud storage bucket immutability lock for 7 years.
2. Conduct full audit of all third-party software log retention settings.
managementResponse: Cloud operations has enabled Object Lock on AWS S3 buckets to enforce 7-year retention compliance.
summaryFinding: Vendor cloud software access logs were purged at 90 days contrary to 7-year regulatory GxP and SOX audit retention mandates.
auditorResponse: Cloud bucket lifecycle configuration audit identified auto-expiration rule misconfiguration applied during October 2025 infrastructure migration.
mitigatingControl: Secondary SIEM ingestion pipeline preserved high-severity auth alerts for 365 days, though granular raw query logs were impacted.
exceptionRemedComments: AWS S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode enabled with immutable 7-year legal hold retention rule.
impactedMrc: MRC-04: Corporate Shared Services & IT Infrastructure

title: Un-reconciled material scrap variance in catheter assembly Line 4
header: Un-reconciled material scrap variance in catheter assembly Line 4
issue:
Un-reconciled material scrap variance of $45,000 logged during Q2 catheter assembly batch run #14.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-04 Section No. [6.2] - Inventory Variance & Scrap Reconciliation Protocol — Material variance thresholds exceeded without supervisory sign-off
2. S-04 Section No. [9] - Batch Integrity & Financial Material Scrap Verification — Lack of mandatory secondary review for scrap exceeding $25,000
originalIssue:
Un-reconciled material scrap variance of $45,000 logged during Q2 catheter assembly batch run #14.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-04 Section No. [6.2] - Inventory Variance & Scrap Reconciliation Protocol — Material variance thresholds exceeded without supervisory sign-off
2. S-04 Section No. [9] - Batch Integrity & Financial Material Scrap Verification — Lack of mandatory secondary review for scrap exceeding $25,000
rootCause: Manual scrap reporting forms were not uploaded to SAP ERP within the required 24-hour shift reconciliation window.
impact: Financial reporting inventory discrepancy of $45,000 across Q2 balance sheet. Increased manual effort required for month-end financial closing.
recommendation:
1. Mandate barcode scanning for all scrap disposals at assembly line stations.
2. Implement real-time SAP inventory posting API.
managementResponse: Plant operations will install barcode scanners at line scrap bins and conduct employee refresher training.
summaryFinding: Physical material scrap worth $45,000 was disposed without timely SAP ERP inventory ledger entry, creating monthly cost-of-goods-sold accounting variance.
auditorResponse: Inventory audit verified a 14-day delay in manual paper scrap log upload, resulting in an un-reconciled variance on the Q2 plant balance sheet.
mitigatingControl: Quarterly physical cycle counts capture cumulative variance before annual financial closing.
exceptionRemedComments: Handheld wireless barcode scanners deployed at scrap staging bins with direct SAP RFC posting.
impactedMrc: MRC-01: Global Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations
